2. The short question that falls for consideration is whether the respondent-land owners are entitled to seek 30% solatium under Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short 1894 Act) on the premise that the expression market value will include (a) the amount of compensation as determined under Section 23 (1); (b) as well as the additional market value calculated at the rate of 12% per annum under Section 23(1-A) of the 1894 Act.

The High Court, in its impugned judgment,
has held the answer in affirmative and, thus, concluded as 17:11:29 IST follows:
22.

In view of above, it can be seen that the amount payable under Section 23(1-A) of the 1894 Act is an additional compensation in respect of acquisition and the same has to be reckoned as part of market value of the land so as the amount of solatium under Section 23(2) of the 1894 Act and interest is payable thereon.
All these components would come together to satisfy the expression awarded amount.

sentences.text: section (1-A) of Section 23, inserted by Act 68 of 1984 provides that in addition to the market value of the land, as provided under Section 23(1), the Court shall, in every case, award an amount calculated at the rate of 12% per annum on such market value for the period commencing on or from the date of publication of the notification under Section 4(1) in respect of such land to the date of award of the Collector or the date of taking possession of the land, whichever is earlier.
The additional amount under Section 23(1-A) and solatium under Section 23(2) are both payable only on the market value determined under Section 23(1) of the Act and not on any other amount.
Solatium under Section 23(2) is not payable on the additional amount nor is additional amount under Section 23(1-A) payable on solatium.
Solatium and additional amount are also not payable on the damages/expenses that may be awarded under second to sixth factors under Section 23(1) of the Act.

4. The decision of this Court in Amarjit Singhs case (supra) was not cited/referred to before the High Court, which has led to the findings by the High Court in paragraph 22, as reproduced above,
being directly in conflict with what this Court has held in Amarjit Singhs case (supra).
5.
For the reasons afore-stated, the instant appeals are allowed.
The impugned judgment of the High Court dated 19.09.2019 is set aside to the extent in which solatium at the rate of 30% is required to be calculated under Section 23(2) of the 1894 Act.

It is clarified that the solatium at the rate of 30%
shall be admissible to the respondents only on the market value as determined under Section 23(1)
of the 1894 Act.

6. As regards to the payment of interest, it goes without saying that the Executing Court shall determine the same, if not already determined, in accordance with Section 34 of the 1894 Act, as explained by this Court in paragraph 12(d) of the decision in Amarjit Singhs case (supra).
The Executing Court shall pass appropriate orders within two months.
The amount so determined, if any, shall be paid by the appellant without any delay.
